tools.name: send_message
tools.description:

tools.name: start_verification
tools.description: Verify a Georgian mobile number: NOTIFY makes a random six-digit code and sends it by SMS with a built-in template. The code is never shown to you: ask the human for the code they received, then call check_verification. A code works for 10 minutes and 5 checks, once; a new start for the same number

tools.name: check_verification
tools.description: Check the code the human typed, for the number the code was sent to. The result is the verification only when it is approved; every other outcome is a tool error with an `error.code`. Let the user in only when a check answers `200` with status `approved`; treat every other answer, a timeout and a ne

tools.name: get_message
tools.description: Read the current state of a message sent with a key of the same project. Poll only while `status` is `queued` or `submitted`: `delivered`, `undeliverable` and `failed` are final, and `unknown` never changes. Wait about 2 seconds before the first read and double the wait each time, up to 30 seconds.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_test_key" references sensitive artifacts (api_key). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "check_verification" appears informational but accepts parameters (code) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_message" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_test_key, send_message, get_message · Private data: create_test_key · Public sink: create_test_key, send_message, start_verification, get_message.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_test_key, send_message, get_message · Private data: create_test_key · Public sink: create_test_key, send_message, start_verification, get_message

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
